title: How Alex West scaled CyberLeads to ~$500k/year by productizing outbound and building systems
summary: Alex tells the story of launching a $2k/month outbound lead-gen service on top of CyberLeads. Early campaigns failed and clients churned, then he documented, automated and simplified his way to results and a viral My First Million mention, only to end up burned out in a "second cage". Lessons cover thinking for yourself, narrowing focus, and distrusting advice that sells a product.

principles.text: Following expert playbooks failed; results only came after thinking for yourself and experimenting broadly.
principles.quote: Looking back, once again, following recipes and playbooks didn't work for me. I only started seeing results when I started thinking for myself.

principles.text: Document every step in exact detail; documentation is like programming and can be automated into a SaaS.
principles.quote: Documenting things step-by-step was exactly like programming. Just in human language and images, instead of code.

principles.text: The behind-the-scenes systems are the real business; the visible product is only the surface.
principles.quote: The real business is not the final product. It's all the behind the scenes stuff that's invisible.

principles.text: Kill complexity and narrow focus: one channel, one language, one target customer made delivery faster and clients happier.
principles.quote: Every process that stayed had to fight for it's life. It was a war against complexity. If it was just ok or good, it would be killed.

principles.text: Clients want results, not effort or leads; refunds can't repair a lost reputation, so guarantees are a weak escape rope.
principles.quote: I could refund money. But I couldn't refund my reputation.

principles.text: Be wary of advice that conveniently matches what the adviser sells; beliefs are only real when they cost you something.
principles.quote: Everyone is talking their own book. And everyone's advice somehow perfectly aligns with what they are selling.
